drafted_from: tool:organize-mail's own row in tools/read-and-write-mail/tool-rows.json and the neutral rows of read-data/neutral.mjs; the answer is the shape the Gmail adapter and the stand-in test of test/mail-adapters.test.mjs produce for this sample input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Star message 18c1a2b3d4e5f601 and mark it read. Use my Gmail account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:organize-mail as that account on the provider gmail and hands back the neutral row.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls the mail provider for one account the connection names and answers the neutral row.
instructions: 1. Connect your mail account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery; the provider is the id in read-data/mail-providers.json that account is on (gmail for it).

2. Say to your AI: "Star message 18c1a2b3d4e5f601 and mark it read." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:organize-mail and the input {"provider":"gmail","connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"message_id":"18c1a2b3d4e5f601","add_labels":["starred"],"remove_labels":["unread"]}.
3. Read what comes back: the labels the message has now.
4. A provider that does not offer the job says so in words and nothing is sent.
